Franklin County, Spring 2026

Payments

Franklin County is set to receive approximately $6.04M in opioid settlement funds from 2022 through 2038. They have received $1.8M to date with $4.25M more anticipated.

Spending Plans

Franklin County has approved and shared 5 spending plans, authorizing 7 unique strategies.

Local governments must approve and share spending plans before spending opioid settlement funds. Local governments may not spend more than the approved amounts (although they may spend less). Exhibit A strategies are high-impact strategies for addressing the opioid overdose epidemic; Exhibit B strategies are from the national settlement agreements and are available to local governments after participating in a Collaborative Strategic Planning process.

See all of Franklin County’s spending authorizations in the Document Library.

Collaborative Strategic Planning Reports and Recommendations

Local govenments that wish to spend opioid settlement funds on any Exhibit B strategies must first engage in the Collaborative Strategic Planning process, resulting in a report and recommendations document submitted to the local governing board. This process is not required before authorizing spending on Exhibit A strategies.

Franklin County has not submitted any report and recommendations documents.

Past Spending

As of Summer 2025, Franklin County has spent $759K on 2 ** Exhibit A strategies ** and no Exhibit B strategies (see plot to right).


Franklin County has spent the most on Collaborative Strategic Planning and Criminal Justice Diversion Programs .


As a state, North Carolina has spent a total of $70.7M ; the top three most-funded strategies are Recovery Support Services ( 56 gov’ts, $19.6M ), Evidence-Based Addiction Treatment ( 39 gov’ts, $8.64M ), and Post-Overdose Response Team ( 36 gov’ts, $8.08M ).

Spending through Summer 2025


This plot averages spending only over governments that have reported spending money on a given strategy. For example, Franklin County has spent $443K on Collaborative Strategic Planning. Statewide, governments have reported funding Collaborative Strategic Planning; the average amount spent between those governments is $126K. This comparison is for informational purposes only, and is not meant to imply any sort of judgement about or relative ranking between settlement-funded programs throughout the state. Comparisons like these often have limited meaning because of the vastly different circumstances in different areas of North Carolina.

Implementation Scale

Local governments are at varying stages of implementing opioid settlement strategies. For each funded strategy, local governments were asked to selec their State of Implementation from a list of 5 options:

  • Exploration and Planning
  • Preparation
  • Initial Implementation
  • Full Implementation
  • Further Expansion
